newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip shares react little to Merrill report.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip shares react little to Merrill report.

text.p: Japanese semiconductor chip shares reacted little to a Merrill Lynch report on Tuesday that said the world memory chip market was turning up, brokers said. But they added there was some bargain-hunting of the shares.
As of 0420 GMT, chip giant NEC Corp was up 10 yen at 1,400. Hitachi Ltd and Toshiba Corp were also 10 yen higher at 1,090 and 703, respectively.

"The direction of the Tokyo market is still unclear and investors are reluctant to buy large issues aggressively," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said. "Chip shares did not move on news of the South Korean production cuts either."

Merrill Lynch said in a report that Samsung Electronics' recent announcement that it would cut back on 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chip (DRAM) production could result in a reduction of worldwide supply.
It said other suppliers in Taiwan and Japan may allow prices to rise without offsetting production increases.

"We estimate that the industry needs a 16 MB price of $9-$10 to provide a satisfactory return," the report said. "In our opinion, the low point of the DRAM cycle has passed and the market is turning up."
South Korean chip maker shares were lifted by the report.
